drafts.title: Keep or improve ride comfort on broken pavement
drafts.description: Customers experience a smooth, non-harsh ride over broken or uneven pavement so long trips and daily roads feel comfortable and composed.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a standardized broken-pavement test track run at 31 mph (50 km/h), a panel of 10 typical customers rates ride harshness ≤3/10 (median) across 5 repeated runs; objective vehicle response shows no increase in occupant-perceived harshness versus current production baseline.
assumptions: Test uses a repeatable, representative rough-road track and the same tires for baseline comparison.
Production suspension hardware and tuning can be adjusted within normal program limits for successor model.
uncertainties: Tuning trade-offs between sporty handling and low-speed harshness may require variant-specific calibration.
Results depend on tire choice and wheel size; criterion assumes standard wheel/tire for the model.

drafts.title: Limit distracting wind noise at highway speeds
drafts.description: At and above typical highway speeds drivers do not hear distracting wind noise; cabin remains composed so conversations and audio remain comfortable.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Interior A-weighted sound pressure level at the driver's ear ≤68 dB(A) at 75 mph (120 km/h) on a baseline highway aero track (windows closed), measured per vehicle acoustic test and validated by a 20-person user panel reporting low wind-noise annoyance in ≥90% of trials.
assumptions: Measurement taken on a standardized aerodynamic test route and on a vehicle in production trim (standard glass/seals).
Target assumes typical factory exterior mirrors and roof attachments for the 5 Series body style.
uncertainties: High-roof accessories, aftermarket roof racks, or some wheel/tire combinations may increase measured noise above target.
Exterior trim changes or different variants (e.g., M Sport) may need variant-specific tuning to meet the same dB target.

drafts.title: Make lane-keeping assist steering smooth and predictable in curves
drafts.description: When lane-keeping assist is active on highways and curved roads, steering corrections are smooth and predictable so drivers do not feel abrupt or nervous interventions.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a 10-run test on representative curved highway segments at 65 mph (105 km/h), a panel of 12 drivers rates steering smoothness ≥8/10 in ≥90% of runs; system-triggered steering interventions judged 'abrupt' by the panel occur in ≤10% of runs.
assumptions: Test uses consistent lane-marking quality and wet/dry surface states representative of typical highways.
Sensor coverage and basic lane-detection performance are at least at current production levels.
uncertainties: Extreme road debris, faded lane markings or unusual road geometry may still cause interventions outside test conditions.
Balancing aggressive lane-keeping with minimal interventions may require regional tuning choices.

drafts.title: Make finding a compatible fast charger simple and reliable on trips
drafts.description: When planning or driving a long trip the vehicle shows only chargers the car can use and lets the customer find a suitable charger quickly, reducing delay and confusion on road trips.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: During route planning for a 200-mile+ trip the vehicle lists only chargers compatible with the selected vehicle variant and connector, including estimated availability/network and payment requirements, with the UI returning results within 30 seconds for ≥90% of queries; in 20 real-world road-trip trials customers locate a compatible charger within 2 minutes in ≥90% of trials.
assumptions: Access to up-to-date public charger databases and roaming/authorization metadata is available at launch.
The vehicle software can be updated to incorporate new networks and connectors post-launch.
uncertainties: Availability of charger networks and roaming agreements is outside vehicle control and may affect user experience.
Third-party network outages or incorrect public data can reduce effective accuracy.

drafts.title: Show charging state at a glance via the external charge-port light
drafts.description: Customers can see whether the vehicle is charging, fully charged, or has a charging fault by looking at the charge port area without using an app or interior screen.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a 50-person user test, participants standing 3 meters from the vehicle correctly identify the external charge port state (charging, full, fault) from the light indication alone in ≥95% of cases (daylight and nighttime scenarios included).
assumptions: Charge-port indicator uses a clear, color-coded and/or steady/blink pattern visible in daylight and night.
Standardized user instructions (quick guide graphic) are provided to customers at delivery.
uncertainties: Very bright sunlight or heavy dirt obscuring the charge port may reduce visibility.
Color-blind users may require non-color cues (blink patterns) to reach the same identification rate.

drafts.title: Offer at least one powertrain variant that delivers ≥600 miles real-world range on a single tank or charge
drafts.description: Customers who need very long single-leg trips have an available 5 Series variant that achieves at least 600 miles of real-world driving range without refueling or recharging.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: At least one available powertrain variant is demonstrated to achieve ≥600 miles (≈965 km) real-world range in a standardized mixed (city/highway) 600-mile validation run (ambient 20–25°C) without refueling/recharging, verified across 3 repeated runs.
assumptions: This requirement may be fulfilled by an internal-combustion, hybrid, or range-extended variant rather than a pure BEV for the successor model.
Real-world validation uses a repeatable route and driving profile representative of customer usage.
Customers accept that very-long-range variants may trade off some efficiency, mass or packaging compared with other variants.
uncertainties: Achieving 600 miles on a pure BEV within 3–5 years depends on battery energy-density and weight trade-offs that are uncertain; execution path may therefore be variant-dependent.
Regional fuel/energy quality and environmental conditions will affect realized range.

drafts.title: Request for Level 3 automated-driving type approval (out of scope: regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers request that the car receives type approval for Level 3 automated driving in Germany. Type-approval and homologation are regulatory activities and not a customer-facing functional requirement to be specified here.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Regulatory type-approval requests are handled outside the scope of customer-facing successor requirements; this draft records the request for program/regulatory teams.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory type-approval / homologation request — out of scope for customer-facing product requirements.

drafts.title: Request that powertrain comply with CARB emission limits in the US (out of scope: regulatory compliance)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the powertrain meets California emission limits in all US states. Emissions type-approval and regulatory compliance are handled by engineering and certification teams.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Regulatory compliance requests are logged for program/certification teams; not specified here as a customer-facing requirement.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory/certification request — out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Request for UN R155 cybersecurity approval (out of scope: regulatory/certification)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the vehicle fulfils UN R155 cybersecurity type approval. Certification is an engineering/regulatory deliverable and not a user-experience requirement defined here.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Regulatory/certification items are tracked with the compliance organization; not defined as a customer-facing successor requirement in this document.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory/certification request — out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Request that the battery complies with the EU battery passport regulation (out of scope: regulatory/certification)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the battery complies with the EU battery passport regulation. This is a certification/data requirement handled by compliance and supply-chain teams.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Logged for compliance and supply-chain follow-up; not specified as a customer-facing feature in this block.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory/data-passport request — out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Request for 800 V electrical architecture (out of scope: engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the car uses an 800 V electrical architecture. This is an engineering architecture choice and therefore an engineering specification rather than a customer-facing requirement.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Technical architecture requests are captured for engineering evaluation; they are out of scope for customer-facing product requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering architecture request (technical spec) — out of scope for customer-facing requirement.

drafts.title: Request for 22 kW onboard AC charger (out of scope: engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the onboard AC charger be upgraded to 22 kW. This is a specific engineering component power-rating request and therefore an engineering specification, not a customer-facing requirement here.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Component power-rating requests are recorded for engineering scoping; out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Component/technical performance request — engineering scope, not a customer-facing requirement.

drafts.title: Request for solid-state cells with 400 Wh/kg (out of scope: engineering/materials spec)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the battery uses solid-state cells with 400 Wh/kg. This is a materials/technology specification and outside the scope of customer-facing requirements.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Materials and cell-chemistry targets are tracked with R&D and battery suppliers; out of scope here.
drafts.scope_reason: Battery chemistry/energy-density specification — engineering/R&D scope, not a customer-facing requirement.

drafts.title: Request for specific front brake-disc diameter (out of scope: engineering/mechanical spec)
drafts.description: Customers request front brake discs of 395 mm diameter. Brake rotor sizing is an engineering/mechanical specification and therefore out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Specific component-dimension requests are recorded for engineering teams; not expressed as a customer-facing requirement here.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific component dimension request — engineering scope, out of customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Request for a named lidar supplier for highway assist (out of scope: supplier selection)
drafts.description: Customers ask that highway assist uses a lidar sensor from a named supplier. Supplier selection is a procurement/engineering decision and not a customer-facing functional requirement.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Supplier preference requests are captured for procurement and engineering; out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Supplier/component choice request — procurement/engineering scope, out of customer-facing requirements.
